questions.stem: Two resistors of 6 ohms and 3 ohms are connected in parallel. What is the total resistance of the combination?
questions.explanation: For parallel resistors: 1/R_total = 1/R1 + 1/R2 = 1/6 + 1/3 = 1/6 + 2/6 = 3/6 = 1/2. So R_total = 2 ohms. Option A (9) adds the resistances, which is the series rule, not parallel. The total resistance in parallel is always less than the smallest individual resistance (3 ohms), which confirms 2 ohms is correct.

questions.stem: A 12 V battery is connected to two lamps in parallel. What is the potential difference across each lamp?

options.text: It depends on the resistance of each lamp

questions.explanation: In a parallel circuit, the potential difference across each branch is the same and equals the supply voltage. So both lamps have 12 V across them. Option A (6 V) would be correct if the lamps were in series and identical. This is a key advantage of parallel circuits — each component receives the full supply voltage.

questions.stem: In a parallel circuit, the current from the battery is 3 A. The current through one branch is 1.2 A. What is the current through the other branch?
questions.explanation: In a parallel circuit, the total current from the battery equals the sum of the currents in each branch: I_total = I1 + I2. So I2 = 3 - 1.2 = 1.8 A. Option B (4.2) adds instead of subtracting. Option A (3 A) gives the total current, not the branch current. This is conservation of charge — current splits at junctions.

questions.stem: Household appliances are connected in parallel rather than in series. Which is NOT an advantage of parallel circuits for household wiring?

options.text: Each appliance receives the full mains voltage
If one appliance fails, the others continue to work
Appliances can be switched on and off independently
The total resistance of the circuit increases when more appliances are added

questions.explanation: Option D is NOT an advantage and is actually incorrect — adding more appliances in parallel DECREASES the total resistance (more parallel paths means lower overall resistance and MORE total current from the supply). Options A, B, and C are all genuine advantages of parallel household wiring. The decrease in total resistance is why adding too many appliances can overload a circuit and blow a fuse.

questions.stem: A 12 V battery is connected to two resistors in parallel: 4 ohms and 12 ohms. What is the total current drawn from the battery?
questions.explanation: In parallel, each branch has 12 V across it. Current through 4 ohm branch: I1 = 12/4 = 3 A. Current through 12 ohm branch: I2 = 12/12 = 1 A. Total current = 3 + 1 = 4 A. Alternatively, find total resistance first: 1/R = 1/4 + 1/12 = 3/12 + 1/12 = 4/12, so R = 3 ohms. Total I = 12/3 = 4 A. Both methods give the same answer.
